claim: The laser warning sign shows the laser's status to people who would not otherwise know it, such as anyone entering the room, and should be placed where it is clearly visible. It carries a remote interlock connector, meant for a switch or chain of switches -- a door switch, for example -- that disables the laser; disconnecting the sign also disables the laser and closes the internal shutter.
validity_conditions: Read from Tweez 305/310 Laser Safety Manual V3.0, November 2022, as installed in C:/Program Files/Aresis/Tweez300/Manuals/ (sha256 264ab54b...): printed page 6 (PDF page 8). Also Tweez 305/310 System Installation Guide, 2021 (sha256 1f664a72..., byte-identical in the installed folder and the lab archive): printed page 13 (PDF page 17). E3 vendor_spec: the manufacturer's statement, not an observation on this bench. The Installation Guide adds that the remote interlock ships short-circuited by default, and that no ordinary network cable may go into the sign's or the unit's RJ45 sockets. KNOWLEDGE, NOT POLICY: this is what the manufacturer says. What any session may do, and every limit anyone here acts on, is the person's, written into the envelope after confirming it on the instrument.
